name: BusyBox
summary: A configurable Unix userland that packages selected applets behind a shared multi-call executable and reusable support code.

features.name: Multi-call applet dispatch
features.description: BusyBox documents a multi-call binary in which the invoked program name or the first argument selects an applet, while the same executable can also be invoked directly as busybox with an applet argument.
benefits: Provides many command entry points through one executable boundary
Allows symlink, hardlink, or direct busybox invocation schemes
costs: Dispatch behavior and applet naming become part of the deployment contract
A single image may carry code and data for multiple selected applets

features.name: Configuration-selected applet set
features.description: The BusyBox source tree uses configuration and generated applet tables to select which applets are built into a particular binary, so the deployed command set is a build-time subset rather than a fixed universal executable.
benefits: Permits small images targeted to a device or recovery environment
Makes feature selection explicit in the build configuration
costs: Different configurations produce different command surfaces to test
Removing an applet can change scripts or operational assumptions

features.name: Shared userland support boundary
features.description: BusyBox applets are organized with common support code in libbb and the source documentation describes applets as sharing code, allowing related command implementations to reuse a common internal support boundary.
benefits: Reduces duplicated implementation across many applets
Creates common helpers for a constrained userland image
costs: Changes to shared helpers can affect many applets
Shared code and global data can increase the footprint of a selected binary

mathematical_views.question: How does an invocation name map to one of the applet behaviors included in a particular BusyBox build?
assumptions: The selected applet names form a finite domain for one build configuration
Dispatch is modeled as a partial function from invocation names to applet entry points
The view abstracts argument parsing, filesystem links, environment, and applet-specific side effects

mathematical_views.question: Which command surface and shared implementation boundary result from selecting an applet set at build time?
assumptions: A build configuration is modeled as a subset of available applets and support components
The comparison concerns packaging and code-sharing boundaries rather than binary-size measurements
Applets can share helpers without becoming semantically equivalent commands

benefits: One executable can expose many command entry points
costs: Invocation-name dispatch adds a packaging and testing contract

benefits: Common helpers reduce repeated applet code
costs: Shared implementation changes widen regression scope
